notes: v0.71.6 — TLS HANDSHAKE FIX, built by CI run 38400225601 from main at d287075. THE ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE of the operator's mobile-only failure was captured on 2026-10-14 by the v0.71.5 forensic diag line, verbatim: CertificateException 'Domain specific configurations require that hostname aware checkServerTrusted(X509Certificate[], String, String) is used'. Android's NSC RootTrustManager refuses a server-trust check without the peer hostname; the Ktor CIO engine the app used since inception builds its SSLEngine anonymously (no peer host), so the TLS handshake died BEFORE the request was written on every send — zero rows server-side, instant failure, while the SAME phone's browser (hostname-aware sockets) chatted fine. This also supersedes the v0.71.5 affinity-pin theory and every earlier theory (VPN, dead server): the app never once completed TLS to the origin on that device. Fix: production engine CIO -> OkHttp (host-named TLS sockets via the platform Conscrypt path) in ServiceLocator (chat) and LiveUpdater (self-update downloads); ktor-client-okhttp added to the version catalog. Honesty fix in the same release: TLS-shaped exceptions (SSLException/CertificateException chain) are rethrown UNWRAPPED by ApiClient, a new SendFailure.TlsHandshake class classifies them, and the notice now reads 'GS could not establish a secure connection: the TLS handshake failed before the request was sent' with the diag suffix — no more mid-turn-cut lie for handshake deaths. Server handshake aligned 0.71.5 -> 0.71.6 (turn-executor.ts + diagnostics). Artifact verified from the release download: com.grapsee.gsai 80/0.71.6 (pyaxmlparser); okhttp3.internal 473 dex hits + io.ktor.client.engine.okhttp 57; baked origin 3 hits; new TLS notice string present; lib/arm64-v8a/libgs_ffi.so 4,590,976 bytes (NDK r25c aarch64); sha256 above; 84,088,502 bytes.
knownLimitations: OpenRouter keypool wiped AGAIN by the platform (all file layers gone; operator's 36 supplied keys unrecoverable from disk). Sends serve via the z-ai fallback route (modelRoute=zai/gs-swift) until the operator re-supplies keys; provision via: bun scripts/provision-keys.ts "key1,key2,..."

backend availability depends on the sandbox dev server being alive; a dead server manifests as instant HTML 502 on sends. v0.71.5's per-launch session rotation means the app self-heals its edge routing after any backend restart.

v0.71.5's 'stale session-affinity pin' root cause was a MISDIAGNOSIS corrected by this release: the real cause was the CIO TLS handshake death (see notes). The rotation and diagnostics shipped in 0.71.5 are what made this diagnosis possible and are kept.
